# SwarmOS TUI v1.26.0

This release collapses the agent's read and search surface onto the shell,
rebuilds the attach/daemon architecture on explicit contracts, and removes
several hot-path costs that were paid on every turn.

It contains a breaking change to the tool surface. See **Breaking changes**.

## Breaking changes

### Search tools are gone; the shell is the search surface

`grep` and the AST/LSP search tools were removed, and `Read` is now image-only.
Reading text and searching a codebase are done with shell commands.

The tools were not removed because they were broken. They were removed because
they duplicated capability the shell already had, at a cost that was being paid
on every request: each tool carries schema text in the system prompt whether or
not it is ever called, and a second, weaker path to a result invites the model
to take it. Collapsing the surface deleted 28,159 lines of tool code and shim
glue against 2,901 added.

`Read` retains the one capability a shell genuinely cannot provide: returning an
image so the model can see it. For text, `sed -n`, `head`, `tail`, `rg`, and
`grep` are the interface.

If you have harness manifests, hooks, or agent prompts that name the removed
tools, they need updating — an unknown tool name in an allow-list no longer
resolves.

## Highlights

### Per-tool cost is measured at the execution chokepoints

Tool cost was previously an argument, not a number. Instrumentation now sits at
the registry and executor chokepoints, so every tool call is attributed with its
real cost rather than estimated from schema size. This is what made the case for
the surface collapse above measurable instead of aesthetic.

### Attach/daemon architecture rebuilt on explicit contracts

The attach daemon was reconstructed over nine phases, starting from written
contracts rather than from the existing implementation.

- **Canonical identities and `AuthenticatedEndpoint`.** Peer identity is derived
  once and carried, instead of being re-derived differently at each call site.
- **Truthful readiness.** Readiness now reports whether the daemon can actually
  serve, not whether its process started. A unified status DTO replaced the
  several partial status shapes that disagreed with each other.
- **Race-safe registry operations** and an explicit lifecycle state machine, so
  a peer cannot be observed in a state it was never in.
- **Reliable `attachclient`** with SSE resume and gap detection, plus WebSocket
  backpressure. A client that misses events now knows it missed them.
- **Signed LAN gossip v2** and presentation-control coexistence, so two
  controllers no longer silently fight over one session.
- **Durable TIL execution journal**, an ADR-006-consistent subset — execution
  survives a restart as a record, not as an inference.
- **`presence` and `supervisor` extracted into their own packages**, `main.go`
  split, and forbidden-import boundary tests added so the layering is enforced
  by the build rather than by convention.

CLI verbs are now canonical `run` and `peer`, with session-scoped workspaces,
approval ownership and timeouts, and lifecycle drain wiring.

### Per-model generation settings

Generation settings (temperature, sampling parameters) are now configurable per
model rather than globally, so switching models no longer silently carries the
previous model's settings into a provider that interprets them differently.

## Performance

Each of these was a cost paid per tick or per turn, not a rare edge case.

- **TUI tick pileup and a defeated render cache.** The render cache was being
  invalidated on a key that changed every frame, so it never hit. Ticks queued
  faster than they drained.
- **The bespoke debug/trace logging subsystem was deleted.** It was env-gated,
  but the gate only suppressed output — the allocations and formatting happened
  regardless of whether anyone was reading.
- **Background output buffers are no longer re-read whole on every tick.**
  Watching a long-running background command re-read the entire accumulated
  buffer each poll, so cost grew with output length.
- **Conversation metadata is cached and reserved directories are no longer
  scanned** during storage operations.
- **The token anomaly detector was removed.** It ran on every turn to report a
  condition that its own output could not distinguish from normal variance.

## Fixes

- **OpenAI SSE streams no longer leak a goroutine.** The stream context was never
  cancelled, so each completed stream left a goroutine parked for the process
  lifetime.
- `bash` retains stdout and stderr on a non-zero exit instead of discarding the
  output that explains the failure, and validates `cwd`.
- Oversized tool output is truncated rather than rejected outright. A result too
  large to return in full is still more useful than no result.
- `TaskManage` list is paginated and its payloads are bounded; key resolution is
  documented.
- `ask_user_question` honors `timeout=0` (no timeout) and accepts the v2 space
  key.
- Hook shell-command classification parses command words instead of matching
  substrings, so a command is no longer classified by a word appearing in an
  argument.
- Skill support files are carried byte-for-byte between packages instead of being
  routed through the model, which silently rewrote text and could not represent
  binary at all.
- Skill relevance ranks on the description text the prompt actually renders,
  rather than on a longer description the model never sees.
- Per-TTL cache splits and segment cache statistics are recorded by provider.
- Release notes are validated in the `metadata` job, before the build matrix
  runs, so a missing notes file fails in seconds instead of after five platform
  builds.

## Verification

The per-tool cost figures come from the instrumentation added in this release,
measured at the registry and executor chokepoints against real usage, and paired
with a usage census drawn from conversation history — not from synthetic calls.
The attach work carries a provenance record: a verification matrix
cross-reference, a phase commit ledger, and a baseline-vs-candidate dogfood probe
are committed alongside the code.

Source release tag: `tui/v1.26.0`
